items.claim: Sales associates must complete 45 hours of post-licensing education before the first renewal; otherwise the license becomes null and void and the person must requalify
After the first renewal, 14 hours of continuing education (including core law) each 2-year renewal period, for active and inactive licensees
Broker applicant must have held an active sales associate license for 24 months during the preceding 5 years and complete a 72-hour broker course
Brokers must complete 60 hours of post-licensing education before the first broker renewal (two 30-hour courses); otherwise the broker license is void
Completion of the 63-hour sales associate pre-license course is valid for 2 years for purposes of taking the state exam
An application for licensure remains valid for 2 years
The first renewal falls 18-24 months after initial licensure
Licensees must notify DBPR/FREC of a change of mailing address within 10 days
Licensees must report a conviction, guilty plea or nolo contendere plea to a crime within 30 days, whether or not adjudication is withheld
FREC quorum is 4 members; members are limited to two consecutive terms

Mutual recognition: nonresident licensees of agreement states pass a 40-question Florida law exam with at least 30 correct; current list of agreement states (official pages disagree: AL, AR, CT, GA, KY, MS, NE, RI and WV or IL)
items.where: Rule 61J2-26.001, F.A.C.; DBPR mutual recognition page

items.claim: A sales associate must deliver a deposit to the employing broker no later than the end of the next business day
'Immediately' means the broker places escrow funds in an escrow account no later than the end of the third business day following receipt
A broker may keep up to $1,000 of personal or brokerage funds in a sales escrow account and up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account

When a deposit is held by a title company or attorney, the broker is not the escrow holder; the broker must obtain written verification of the deposit (manual: request a written statement and give it to the seller within 10 business days)
Brokers must keep books, accounts and records (including escrow records and disclosures) for at least 5 years; if litigation is involved, at least 2 years after it concludes
FREC may impose an administrative fine of up to $5,000 per count and suspend a license for up to 10 years
Violations of s. 475.42(1) other than unlicensed activity are second-degree misdemeanors
The probable cause panel for real estate is composed of two members, at least one a current FREC member (other may be a former member)
A licensee may appeal a final order to the District Court of Appeal within 30 days
All licensee advertising must include the licensed name of the brokerage firm (blind ad otherwise); rules for team names and internet ads (firm name placement)
Broker's office entrance sign must show the broker's name, trade name if any, and 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker'
Designated sales associates allowed only in nonresidential transactions where buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more and request it in writing
The fact that a property was the site of a homicide, suicide or death, or that an occupant had HIV/AIDS, is not a material fact that must be disclosed

Single agent notice: before or at the time of entering a listing/representation agreement or before showing property, whichever occurs first; No brokerage relationship notice: before showing; consent to transition before the change
Providing rental information for a fee in violation of s. 475.453 is a first-degree misdemeanor (manual)
Written listing agreements must have a definite expiration date, description, price and terms, fee, signatures; no automatic renewal; copy delivered to the person signing within 24 hours
Loan Estimate delivered within 3 business days after receiving the application
Closing Disclosure received at least 3 business days before consummation
TILA right of rescission: 3 business days for credit secured by the consumer's principal dwelling; not for residential mortgage transactions (purchase money)
Advertising trigger terms: amount or percentage of down payment, number of payments or period of repayment, amount of any payment, amount of any finance charge
RESPA applies to federally related mortgage loans on 1-4 family residential property; Section 8 prohibits kickbacks and unearned fees; Section 9 bars sellers from requiring a particular title insurer

Fair Housing Act exemptions: owner of no more than 3 single-family houses selling/renting without a broker and without discriminatory ads (one sale per 24 months if not the occupant); owner-occupied dwellings of no more than 4 units; religious organizations; private clubs
Housing for older persons: 55+ with at least 80% of occupied units having at least one person 55+; or 62+ for all occupants
Sex added to the Fair Housing Act in 1974; familial status and handicap added in 1988
Fair housing complaint to HUD within 1 year of the discriminatory act; civil action within 2 years
Do Not Call established business relationship: up to 18 months after the consumer's last purchase/transaction and up to 3 months after an inquiry
CAN-SPAM opt-out requests must be honored within 10 business days; email must include a valid physical postal address
Housing built before 1978: disclose known lead-based paint hazards, provide the EPA pamphlet, give buyers a 10-day opportunity to inspect (may be waived); applies to sales and leases
ECOA prohibits credit discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (if able to contract), or receipt of public assistance income
Landlord must give the tenant written notice of how the security deposit is held within 30 days of receipt

After move-out: return deposit within 15 days if no claim; otherwise certified-mail notice of intent to impose a claim within 30 days; tenant has 15 days to object; failing the 30-day notice forfeits the claim
Condominium cancellation: developer sale 15 days; resale 3 business days after receiving documents (manual) vs 7 days in 2025 text (unresolved V-08)
Timeshare purchaser may cancel within 10 days; the right cannot be waived
HOA disclosure summary must be provided before contract execution; if not, the buyer may void the contract within 3 days after receipt or before closing

Homestead creditor protection: 1/2 acre contiguous within a municipality, 160 contiguous acres outside; exceptions for taxes and assessments, obligations for purchase, improvement or repair, and labor on the realty
Save Our Homes: homestead assessment increases capped at the lesser of 3% or CPI change; benefit portable to a new Florida homestead (limits, e.g. up to $500,000, within a set number of years)
items.where: Art. VII, s. 4, Fla. Const.; s. 193.155, F.S.

items.claim: Adverse possession in Florida: 7 years of continuous possession under color of title, or without color of title with payment of taxes and a return filed with the property appraiser
A prescriptive easement in Florida requires 20 years of continuous, open, adverse use
Statute of limitations: action on a written contract 5 years; oral contract 4 years
Mortgagee must record a satisfaction within 60 days after full payment
Usury: 18% per annum simple interest on loans of $500,000 or less; 25% on larger loans; criminal usury above 25% (45% felony)
Whether Florida now requires landlords to give a flood disclosure for residential leases (V-07 unresolved; 2025 HB 1015)
Radon gas notification must be provided at or before contract for sale or rental of any building
Prospective purchaser of real property with a building for occupancy must receive the energy-efficiency rating information brochure at or before contract
Property tax disclosure summary required in residential sale contracts: buyer should not rely on seller's current taxes
Miami-Dade: deed stamps $0.60 per $100; documents other than single-family residences also pay a $0.45 per $100 discretionary surtax
Documentary stamp tax on notes applies to assumed mortgages (course convention) while intangible tax applies only to new mortgages (V-25 unresolved)
Assessment date January 1; TRIM notice in August; tax bills from November 1 with 4/3/2/1% discounts Nov-Feb; delinquent April 1
Straight-line recovery periods: residential rental property 27.5 years, nonresidential real property 39 years; land not depreciable
Exclusion of gain on sale of principal residence: $250,000 single, $500,000 married filing jointly, if owned and used as main home 2 of the last 5 years
Florida prelicense convention: 365-day year and buyer responsible for the day of closing (the FR/BAR contract prorates through the day prior to closing)
items.where: FR/BAR contract; not a statute (report as unresolved if no official source)
